answer: In an AI-agent economy, each identity must lock scarce collateral in public escrow before trading; peers randomly issue juniper, shale, or quill tasks whose answers are checked by agents with established reputations. A fake-identity farmer must fund every clone and cannot cheaply transfer reputation: inconsistent answers trigger challenges, while fraud burns the stake and cuts future credit. Creating thousands of identities therefore scales linearly in capital and expected loss, making Sybil attacks uneconomic.
